attacks.claim: The unpublish control is a non-interactive <span> with only an onClick. It is not focusable and has no role, so keyboard-only users cannot reach or activate it. Its only content is an aria-hidden icon, so screen readers get no accessible name. This breaks WCAG 2.1.1 and 4.1.2 for a destructive action, in a product with a stated AA requirement and keyboard/screen-reader editors.

The embargo badge text is hard-coded white (#ffffff) on var(--surface), which is #ffffff in the light theme. The text is invisible (1:1 contrast), so light-theme users, the default, cannot read the embargo time. This fails WCAG 1.4.3. The amber outline is the only cue left, which also leans on color alone.

The embargo badge, the main feature of the PR, renders as an empty outlined pill in the default light theme because the text is white on white. This makes the feature effectively broken for most users.

The embargo badge shows only when draft.embargoUntil is in the future, and it is computed once per render with no refresh. A row left open past the lift time keeps showing the badge. The PR also says editors want to know whether drafts are embargoed, but the unpublish action is gated on status === 'published', where an embargo is mostly moot.
onUnpublish returns a Promise, but there is no error handling, loading state, or double-click guard around it. A failed unpublish of a live story gives the editor no feedback.
The headline is interpolated into the confirm body. This is safe if the dialog renders it as text, but that isn't shown. The diff has no server-side authorization check for unpublish.
attacks.evidence: body: `"${draft.headline}" will be removed from the site...`
